## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Goliyāni Sutta* (MN 69, PTS MN i 469), also titled *Goliyānisutta* and translated as *With Gulissāni*, is a discourse in the Majjhimanikāya [SuttaCentral]. The sutta concerns a monk who visits the community from the wilderness but fails to behave appropriately; in response, the Venerable Sāriputta delivers instructions detailing how a mendicant should properly conduct himself, whether residing in the forest or dwelling in town among the monastic community [SuttaCentral]. In modern studies on Buddhist ethics, the text is cited specifically for its guidelines on how a forest-dwelling monk (*āraññaka*) is expected to behave when returning temporarily or permanently to live within the monastic order [Löhr 2004]. English translations have been published by I.B. Horner and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

A full parallel to the sutta is preserved in the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* as MĀ 26 (T 26) [SuttaCentral], a correspondence supported by DharmaNexus alignment data [DharmaNexus]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus also reveals extensive internal parallels across the Pali Canon, most prominently with the *Mahāhatthipadopama Sutta* (MN 28), the *Kīṭāgiri Sutta* (MN 70), various sections of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 3, AN 5, AN 8, AN 9, AN 10), and Vinaya texts including the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 46), *Vattakkhandhaka*, and *Mahākhandhaka*, as well as minor alignments with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) and a Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) [DharmaNexus].
